build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: after picture 4: the unpacker reads on to the end of its 3-sector window, and no directory entry on side 3 says where the picture's packed bytes end. The picture code stops at $CD95, and nothing reads these

comments.text: Picture 4's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$004D, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0021, channel 2's script at +$0037 and 0 for channel 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 6 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 7, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 3, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1. One pass takes 14 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 7 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 15, frame 3 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 3 then 1. One pass takes 21 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 7 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 25, frame 6 then 1, frame 7 then 1, frame 8 then 1, frame 8 then 1, frame 7 then 1, frame 6 then 1. One pass takes 31 steps.

Picture 4's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $07 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 30 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 20 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 4, named by channel 1's entry 1 and channel 2's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 3 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 3 bitmap bytes in all, in column 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 3 and 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 7 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 9 to 11. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 9 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 16 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 9 to 11. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 2 and 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 3 bitmap bytes in all, in column 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 3 and 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 7 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 6 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 4, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 8 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 15 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 6 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
